story_variants.en:
## Vaathiyaar's Advanced Decoder

Vaathiyaar upgrades the magnifying glass to a high-tech scanner. "Basic regex finds patterns. Advanced regex **transforms** text, **extracts** structured data, and handles edge cases with lookahead and lookbehind."

### Advanced Features

| Feature | Syntax | Purpose |
|---------|--------|----------|
| Named Group | `(?P<name>...)` | Label captured groups |
| Lookahead | `(?=...)` | Match only if followed by |
| Lookbehind | `(?<=...)` | Match only if preceded by |
| Non-capturing | `(?:...)` | Group without capturing |
| `re.sub` | `re.sub(pattern, repl, text)` | Find and replace |
| `re.compile` | `re.compile(pattern)` | Pre-compile for speed |

### Named Groups

```python
pattern = r'(?P<year>\d{4})-(?P<month>\d{2})-(?P<day>\d{2})'
match = re.search(pattern, '2025-03-27')
print(match.group('year'))  # 2025
```

> **Key Concept:** Named groups make your regex self-documenting. Instead of `match.group(1)`, use `match.group('year')` — much clearer for maintenance.
story_variants.ta:
## Vaathiyaar மேம்படுத்தப்பட்ட டிகோட்டர்

Vaathiyaar மூன்றாம் நிலை பார்வையாளரை உயர் தொழில்நுட்ப ஸ்கேனராக மேம்படுத்துகிறார். "அடிப்படை regex பாட்டர்களைக் கண்டறிகிறது. மேம்படுத்தப்பட்ட regex **உரையை மாற்றுகிறது**, **அமைப்பான தரவை பிடிக்கிறது**, மேலும் lookahead மற்றும் lookbehind உடன் விளிம்பு நிலைகளைக் கையாளுகிறது."

### மேம்படுத்தப்பட்ட அம்சங்கள்

| அம்சம் | தொடரியல் | நோக்கம் |
|---------|--------|----------|
| பெயரிடப்பட்ட குழு | `(?P<name>...)` | பிடிக்கப்பட்ட குழுக்களை சிட்டையிடுகிறது |
| Lookahead | `(?=...)` | பின்னர் வரும்போது மட்டுமே பொருந்தும் |
| Lookbehind | `(?<=...)` | முன்னர் வந்தால் மட்டுமே பொருந்தும் |
| பிடிக்காத குழு | `(?:...)` | பிடிக்காத குழு |
| `re.sub` | `re.sub(pattern, repl, text)` | கண்டறிந்து மாற்றுகிறது |
| `re.compile` | `re.compile(pattern)` | வேகத்திற்காக முன்பதிலேயே தொகுக்கிறது |

### பெயரிடப்பட்ட குழுக்கள்

```python
pattern = r'(?P<year>\d{4})-(?P<month>\d{2})-(?P<day>\d{2})'
match = re.search(pattern, '2025-03-27')
print(match.group('year'))  # 2025
```

> **முக்கிய கருத்து:** பெயரிடப்பட்ட குழுக்கள் உங்கள் ரெக்குஎக்ஸை தன்னியக்க ஆவணப்படுத்துகின்றன. `match.group(1)` என்பதற்குப் பதிலாக `match.group('year')` — பராமரிப்புக்கு மிகவும் தெளிவானது.

## వాథియార్ యొక్క అధునాతన డీకోడర్

వాథియార్ గ్లాస్ను హైటెక్ స్కానర్కు అప్గ్రేడ్ చేస్తుంది. "బేసిక్ రెగెక్స్ నమూనాలను కనుగొంటుంది. అధునాతన రెగెక్స్ **ట్రాన్స్ఫర్మ్లు **టెక్స్ట్,**ఎక్స్ట్రాక్ట్స్ ** నిర్మాణాత్మక డేటా, మరియు లుక్హెడ్ మరియు లుక్బ్యాక్తో అంచు కేసులను నిర్వహిస్తుంది. "

### ఆధునిక లక్షణాలు

### పేరు పెట్టబడిన సమూహాలు

```python
pattern = r'(?P<year>\d{4})-(?P<month>\d{2})-(?P<day>\d{2})'
match = re.search(pattern, '2025-03-27')
print(match.group('year'))  # 2025
```

> ** కీ భావనః** పేరుతో కూడిన సమూహాలు మీ రెజిక్స్ను స్వీయ-పత్రీకరించడానికి సహాయపడతాయి. `match.group(1) `కాకుండా, నిర్వహణ కోసం`match.group('year') `  ను ఉపయోగించండి.

q.en: What is the advantage of re.compile()?

en: Pre-compiles pattern for faster repeated use

under_the_hood.summary: Groups record start and end positions while the engine matches, lookarounds run a sub-pattern at the current position without consuming characters, and re.sub stitches the output from unmatched gaps and replacements.

steps.title: Groups store positions, not copies
steps.body: `(?P<user>\w+)@(?P<host>[\w.]+)` makes the engine save a start mark when it enters each group and an end mark when it leaves. The Match object keeps these index pairs; `m.group('user')` slices the original string with them, and `m.span('host')` shows the raw positions.

steps.title: Lookahead peeks without moving
steps.body: `\d+(?= rupees)` matches digits only if ' rupees' follows. At the end of the digits the engine runs the lookahead sub-pattern at that position; if it succeeds, the engine returns to the same position and continues. The text ' rupees' is checked but not part of the match.

steps.title: Lookbehind checks backwards
steps.body: `(?<=Rs\.)\d+` steps back from the current position and checks that 'Rs.' ends exactly here. Python's re requires lookbehind to have a fixed width so it knows how far to step back; `(?<=a+)` raises an error. Negative versions `(?!...)` and `(?<!...)` succeed when the sub-pattern fails.

steps.title: re.sub builds the result in pieces
steps.body: `re.sub(r'(\d+)-(\d+)', r'\2-\1', text)` scans left to right for non-overlapping matches. For each one it appends the text before the match, then the replacement with `\2` and `\1` filled from the groups. After the last match it appends the remainder and joins everything into a new string.

stepDescriptions.description: No more matches: join pieces -> 'a 20-10 b 4-3'.

steps.title: Compiled patterns save the parse
steps.body: Inside a loop, `PHONE = re.compile(...)` defined once and reused avoids even the cache lookup and keeps the pattern in one named place. The compiled object also offers `finditer`, which yields Match objects lazily.

under_the_hood.takeaway: Groups are bookmarks into the original string, lookarounds are checks that do not move the cursor, and sub is a scan that copies gaps and builds replacements. With those three ideas, advanced patterns become predictable.
